submission.justification: Sensitivity scan (statistical uncertainty only, from simulate_significance): S3 peaks at about 4.04 sigma (60% efficiency; 4.02 at 50%), S2 at 3.37 sigma (50%; 3.07 at 30%, 3.24 at 70%), and S1 at 2.61 sigma (50%). S3 is the most sensitive, but it uses jet substructure variables. The data/MC validation-region agreement that the hard 10% constraint depends on is not reported in any project document or tool I could access, so compliance cannot be verified for any strategy. S3's jet-substructure inputs are the most likely source of mismodelling, so I recommend S2 at 50% efficiency as the strategy most likely to pass the hard constraint. It uses kinematic variables only and gives about 3.4 sigma, roughly 0.65 sigma below S3. This recommendation is conditional: the validation-region check for S2's kinematic inputs must still be run and must show at most 10% disagreement before unblinding. If S3's jet-substructure variables pass that check, S3 at about 50-60% efficiency would be preferable for the higher significance. The 50% working point is not a fine optimum for S2; I only sampled 30, 50 and 70%.
